name: Szeged
tagline: The sunniest city in Hungary, a university town on the Tisza with a twin-towered Votive Church, Art Nouveau facades, fish soup and paprika.
highlight: The Votive Church's twin spires above Dóm Square, the heart of the city.
shortDescription: A lively southern city rebuilt after a great flood in 1879, with the Votive Church, Reök Palace, riverside promenades, halászlé fish soup and Szeged paprika and salami.
metaDescription: A Szeged travel guide: Votive Church, Reök Palace, Dóm Square, Tisza riverfront, fish soup, paprika and salami, thermal baths, how to get there from Budapest and a one-to-two-day plan.

image.alt: The twin-towered Votive Church of Szeged

intro: Szeged is the largest city in southern Hungary, with about 160,000 people, and it sits on the Tisza river near the borders with Serbia and Romania. It receives more hours of sunshine than any other Hungarian city, and it is a lively university town, with students making up a big part of the population. It is known as the City of Sunshine.

In 1879, a devastating flood destroyed most of the city. Rebuilding created a rational plan of wide boulevards and ring roads, with grand Art Nouveau and eclectic buildings, such as the colourful Reök Palace. The centrepiece is the Votive Church, a twin-towered brick cathedral built after the flood, whose 91-metre spires dominate Dóm Square, where an open-air festival of theatre and music is held each summer.

Szeged is also a food city. It is the home of halászlé, the paprika fish soup made with river carp and catfish, of Pick salami, and of one of the country's main paprika-growing areas. It makes a good stop on the way to or from Serbia, and one or two days is enough.
